summary:
Mission Mars: transforms NASA's Martian imagery, topography, atmospheric telemetry, and historical hardware archives into a playable, browser-based 3D open-world survival, navigation, and engineering game set in Jezero Crater (18.4447°N, 77.4508°E).

Instead of inspecting flat 2D GIS maps, users seamlessly switch via an orbital sky-camera wheel between the Perseverance Rover, the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, and an on-foot EVA Astronaut in 0.38g gravity. A real-time 60×60 A* Terrain Pathfinder evaluates slope gradients across a modelled Jezero terrain to project glowing 3D route chevrons around lethal >18° cliffs and toward a Lava Tube Radiation Shelter during 5-star Dust Storms. Players fire a live SuperCam LIBS Laser Spectrometer (240–850 nm atomic emission spectra), customize rover mass/power trade-offs in the Octavia Engineering Garage, listen to DSN Radio FM terrain sonification, and locate 5 real discarded NASA artifacts to Preserve or Salvage.
details:
Mission Mars:

An Interactive 3D Mars Exploration and Survival Simulator

What Problem Does Mission Mars Solve?

Exploring Mars presents a complex, high-stakes challenge involving terrain stability, solar irradiance, regional dust storms, extreme temperatures (as low as −86°C), and cosmic radiation exposure.

At the same time, thousands of kilograms of NASA entry, descent, and landing (EDL) hardware remain scattered across the Martian surface. These artifacts represent both valuable space heritage and potential in-situ resources for future human missions.

Traditional 2D contour maps struggle to communicate the three-dimensional nature of these hazards, making Martian exploration difficult to visualize for students, mission planners, and citizen scientists.

Mission Mars: addresses this challenge by transforming Jezero Crater into an interactive, 60 FPS, WebGL-powered 3D open world.

Inspired by modern open-world games, the simulator combines realistic Martian terrain, scientific exploration, survival mechanics, and intuitive gameplay systems—including a heads-up display (HUD), radar minimap, vehicle switching, and interactive mission objectives.

The result is an accessible, scientifically grounded environment where users can explore Mars, analyze real mission data, and experience the engineering challenges of planetary exploration.

Core Scientific and Technical Systems

1. Martian Terrain Modeling and Slope-Safe Pathfinding

60×60 MOLA/HiRISE Digital Elevation Model (DEM) with A Navigation*

The simulator recreates major geological landmarks in Jezero Crater, including:

  • Octavia E. Butler Landing Site
  • Neretva Vallis River Delta Escarpment
  • Kodiak Butte
  • Belva Crater
  • South Seitah Ridge

Key capabilities:

  • Terrain Analysis: Models Martian topography using a 60×60 navigation grid.
  • Slope Detection: Calculates terrain gradients (∇z) using central finite differences.
  • Intelligent Pathfinding: Implements A* navigation with penalties for slopes exceeding 18°, helping identify energy-efficient routes for astronauts and rovers.
  • High-Resolution Surface Detail: Adds runtime terrain relief sampled at 128×128 resolution from NASA’s HiRISE/CTX Jezero orbital mosaic (PIA23720). This provides texture-derived terrain approximations rather than survey-grade elevation measurements.
  • 3D Route Visualization: Displays navigation routes through a tilted radar minimap and glowing 3D chevron arrows projected directly onto the Martian surface.

Interactive Tactical Map (M)

A full-screen tactical map allows users to switch between three scientific visualization layers:

  1. MOLA Elevation: Martian surface topography.
  2. Slope Hazard: Terrain regions exceeding the 18° safety threshold.
  3. SWIM Subsurface Water-Ice Depth: Water-ice distribution and depth visualization.

2. Three Playable Exploration Units

Seamless Vehicle Switching with Cinematic Sky-Camera Transitions (1 / 2 / 3 / TAB)

Players can control three exploration units, each designed for different mission objectives.

Perseverance Rover — 6×6 Exploration Vehicle

A six-wheeled robotic exploration platform featuring:

  • Rocker-bogie suspension with terrain-responsive pitch and roll.
  • Persistent wheel tracks across the Martian regolith.
  • Volumetric headlights (L) for low-light navigation.
  • Interactive SuperCam laser spectroscopy (SPACE).
  • Surface traversal and scientific data collection.

Ingenuity Mars Helicopter

An aerial reconnaissance platform featuring:

  • Coaxial, counter-rotating rotor simulation.
  • Flight controls (SHIFT / C).
  • Aerial scouting of steep crater rims, dune fields, and hazardous terrain.
  • Elevated observation of otherwise inaccessible locations.

Commander Val — EVA Astronaut

A playable astronaut designed for human exploration scenarios.

Features include:

  • On-foot exploration under Martian gravity (0.38g / 3.721 m/s²).
  • Surface inspection and environmental interaction.
  • Seamless vehicle embarkation and disembarkation (F).
  • Exploration of archaeological sites and potential survival resources.

3. Space Archaeology and Environmental Weathering

“Abandoned but Not Forgotten” — Preserving the History of Mars Exploration

The simulator features five historical NASA mission artifacts and locations associated with Jezero Crater:

  1. Perseverance Heat Shield Impact Site — The rover’s approximately 4.5 m thermal protection system.
  2. Aeroshell Backshell and Parachute Wreckage — Remnants of the spacecraft’s supersonic parachute and descent hardware.
  3. Sky Crane Descent Stage Crash Site — The discarded descent stage used during Perseverance’s landing.
  4. Ingenuity Flight 72 Final Airfield — The helicopter’s final landing area near Valinor Hills.
  5. Three Forks Sample Depot — Titanium sample tubes deposited for potential future retrieval.

Each location provides an interactive opportunity to investigate the long-term effects of the Martian environment on human-made materials.

Environmental degradation simulations include:

  • Ultraviolet-induced polymer degradation.
  • Perchlorate-rich dust accumulation.
  • Micrometeorite surface pitting.
  • Long-term exposure to the Martian atmosphere since February 2021.

Interactive Resource Decisions

At each archaeological site, players face a choice:

  • Preserve as a Heritage Monument: Protect historically significant artifacts for future scientific and cultural study.
  • Recycle for Habitat Survival: Recover potentially useful titanium, sensors, and other materials to support future human exploration.

This system introduces ethical trade-offs between space heritage preservation and resource utilization.

4. SuperCam Spectroscopy and Engineering Upgrades

SuperCam LIBS Atomic Spectrum Analyzer

The simulator includes an interactive Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) system inspired by NASA’s Perseverance SuperCam instrument.

When activated, the laser generates a simulated atomic emission spectrum covering 240–850 nm.

The analyzer visualizes spectral signatures associated with:

  • Silicon (Si)
  • Iron (Fe)
  • Magnesium (Mg)
  • Calcium (Ca)
  • Titanium (Ti)
  • Hydrogen (Hα), including water-related spectral interpretation

A simulated Mastcam-Z false-color micro-imaging feed appears in a Picture-in-Picture (PiP) display, providing additional visual context for geological analysis.

Octavia Engineering Garage

Scientific exploration rewards players with Science Data (MB), which can be used to unlock advanced engineering upgrades inspired by real NASA technologies.

Available upgrades include:

1. NASA Glenn Nitinol Shape-Memory Mesh Tires

  • Improved terrain adaptability.
  • Enhanced durability on rocky surfaces.
  • Modified traction and slope performance.

2. Dual MMRTG + Triple-Junction GaAs Solar Wing

  • Hybrid nuclear and solar power configuration.
  • Increased available energy.
  • Additional mass and power-management trade-offs.

3. SuperCam Raman + RIMFAX Radar

  • Enhanced mineralogical analysis.
  • Subsurface geological investigation.
  • Expanded scientific sensing capabilities.

4. Silica Aerogel + Polyethylene Crew Shielding

  • Improved thermal insulation.
  • Enhanced radiation protection.
  • Additional vehicle mass and mobility considerations.

Every upgrade introduces engineering trade-offs involving:

  • Mass (kg)
  • Power consumption and generation (W)
  • Maximum vehicle speed
  • Safe operating slope
  • Exploration capabilities

This system encourages players to balance scientific performance, energy efficiency, mobility, and astronaut safety.

5. Martian Environment, Survival, and Telemetry

Dynamic Martian Sol Cycle

The simulator recreates environmental conditions across a Martian day, allowing players to experience changing illumination, temperature, and solar energy availability.

Martian Noon

  • Solar irradiance: 540 W/m²
  • Temperature: −22°C
  • Bright daytime surface conditions

Blue Martian Sunset

  • Solar irradiance: 145 W/m²
  • Temperature: −61°C
  • Atmospheric scattering produces Mars’s characteristic blue sunset.

Martian Night

  • Solar irradiance: 0 W/m²
  • Temperature: −86°C
  • Star-filled sky with an orbiting Phobos simulation.

These environmental states affect visibility, exploration conditions, and energy-management decisions.

Lava Tube Radiation Shelter

A basalt lava tube provides a simulated underground refuge from hazardous surface conditions.

Features include:

  • Radiation shielding with a simplified 0.00 mSv gameplay exposure indicator.
  • Protection during severe, five-star dust storms.
  • A potential survival location for future astronaut missions.

Deep Space Network Telemetry Sonification

The simulator includes DSN Radio FM, a procedural audio system built with the WebAudio API.

Instead of relying on prerecorded audio, the system converts simulated terrain telemetry into ambient sound.

Sonification inputs include:

  • MOLA elevation data.
  • Terrain slope gradients.
  • Navigation-related environmental parameters.

These values dynamically influence synthesized frequencies and layered audio tracks, creating an immersive representation of Martian terrain through sound.

Technology Stack

3D Rendering and Simulation

Three.js + WebGL

  • Interactive 3D Martian environment.
  • Terrain rendering and vehicle animation.
  • Lighting, environmental effects, and simulation mechanics.
  • Real-time rendering targeting 60 FPS.

Scientific Visualization

HTML5 Canvas 2D

  • Radar minimap.
  • Tactical digital elevation map.
  • LIBS atomic spectrum oscilloscope.
  • Mastcam-Z Picture-in-Picture visualization.

Audio

WebAudio API

  • Procedural sound generation.
  • Oscillator-based frequency synthesis.
  • Multi-track telemetry sonification.
  • Zero-dependency ambient audio engine.

Controls and Accessibility

  • Keyboard and Mouse: Desktop exploration and interaction.
  • Mobile Touch D-Pad: Responsive controls for touch-enabled devices (pointer: coarse).
  • HTML5 Gamepad API: Support for Xbox and PlayStation controllers.
  • Autonomous Judge Tour Mode (P): Automated demonstration of the simulator’s major features.

Project Impact

Mission Mars: transforms planetary science into an interactive exploration experience.

By combining real NASA mission references, terrain-aware navigation, simulated scientific instruments, environmental survival systems, and open-world gameplay, the project makes complex Martian exploration challenges easier to visualize and understand.

Rather than simply viewing Mars through static images and elevation maps, users can navigate its terrain, investigate historical artifacts, analyze geological materials, and make engineering decisions inspired by the challenges of future human missions.

The goal is to make Mars exploration more accessible, engaging, and educational—bridging the gap between scientific data and hands-on discovery.
